checksums.name: image_sum32le_trailing
checksums.formula_detail: stored = (sum of 4095 u32_le words at copy offsets 0x0000..0x3FFB) mod 2^32, stored u32_le at copy offset 0x3FFC. First 0x1C00 bytes are zero in the sample, so the sum equals the sum over 0x1C00..0x3FFB. Falsified: including the stored word (0x5F6F2D6A), CRC32 (0xB7EE5B0A), XOR32 (0x0E06350D), sum16 (0x012EC5BD).

io_driver_functions.notes: SRAM_V112-style read: sets wait-state bits (|3), copies an access stub to the stack and executes it via 0x0816860c. Used for SRAM->buffer reads (0x400 chunks in the checksum verifier, 0x100 pages in the writer) and for 4-byte status-word reads. Argument order (src, dst, len).
SRAM byte-at-a-time write: explicit loop *dst++ = *src++ after wait-state setup; byte stores are mandatory for GBA SRAM. Sole caller is the whole-image writer.
SRAM verify/compare variant of 0x08168490 that returns the stub result; called only with length 0x28 (40). Zero return = region matches. Its non-zero result triggers whole-image repair in 0x0809dbe4.

Checksum verifier: allocates 0x400 buffer (0x08082d74), reads SRAM 0x0E000000 in 16x0x400 chunks via 0x08168490, accumulates sum32le, frees buffer (0x08082d5c), reads stored u32 from the image tail and returns computed == stored. Stored-word address is an unresolved literal-pool value, identified as copy offset 0x3FFC by elimination against the real .sav.

Whole-image SRAM writer/serializer: (ram_src, 0x0E000000, 0x4000); pages 0x100 bytes at a time through a staging buffer (0x08168490 RAM->buffer, 0x081684f4 buffer->SRAM), alloc/free via 0x08082d74/0x08082d68. The only SRAM write path in the corpus; no partial writes exist.

Validate-or-repair loader: verifies the 0x28-byte signature (0x08168564) and the image checksum (0x0809dea0), reads/compares a standalone u32 status word, and on any failure rewrites all 0x4000 bytes from the in-RAM template via 0x0809e00c, then re-verifies. Returns the status word to its caller. RAM template base and status-word offset are unresolved literal-pool placeholders.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Scene/object constructor reached via unrecovered jumptable dispatch (no static caller in corpus). Calls FUN_0809dbe4() once during construction and branches on its returned status word: equal to an unresolved constant -> object fields +0x78=2 (u16), +0x7A=1 (u8); zero -> +0x78=1, +0x7A=0; otherwise -> error path disposing the object and building a replacement via FUN_08082d84 + 0x0809e2bc.
caller_chains.how_mapped: callgraph.json lists 0x08112284 as the sole caller of 0x0809dbe4; confirmed textually in ghidra/decompiled.c (callgraph records no callees for the save core because calls are func_ placeholders, so textual search for both FUN_/func_ spellings was used for every hop). This caller mutates only its own object, never the save struct.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Repair path: taken when the 0x28-byte signature verify or the image checksum fails, or the standalone u32 status word differs from its expected RAM-side value. Rewrites the entire 0x4000-byte SRAM image from the in-RAM template struct (source operand unresolved), then re-verifies signature and checksum.
ram_fields_updated: entire 0x4000-byte SRAM image (all fields in the field map)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Textual call func_0x0809e00c(template, 0x0E000000, 0x4000) inside FUN_0809dbe4 in decompiled.c/save_related_functions.c; 0x0809e00c has no other caller in the 191 traced functions (callgraph.json shows no recorded callers due to func_ placeholder calls). This is the only flush of the save struct in the corpus.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Validation path: checksum verification of the on-cartridge image during load; result combined with the signature verify decides whether the repair chain (0x0809e00c) fires.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Textual call func_0x0809dea0() inside FUN_0809dbe4; FUN_0809dea0 internally uses FUN_08082d74 for its 0x400 scratch buffer and FUN_08082d5c to free it. The allocator/free pair (0x08082cac/0x08082c10 underneath) are generic heap services with many non-save callers; only these buffer uses are on the save path.

fields.name: sentinel_records_999

observed_values.sav-00-f990.sav: 34 blocks of 30x u16_le 0x03E7 (999) = bytes e703 x30 (60 bytes), stride 0x78 (120): blocks at 0x1C64 + i*0x78 for i=0..33, each followed by 60 zero bytes except after the last block

fields.evidence: Exact-match Python scan for (e703)*30 found 34 hits at a constant 120-byte stride; bytes themselves are verified. Record semantics (34x120-byte records vs interleaved arrays) and the meaning of sentinel 999 are undetermined from a single default-heavy sample.

fields.name: post_array_word_a
fields.evidence: First word after the sentinel array at copy 0x2C18. Pair 1,2 with post_array_word_b suggests small enum/count fields; semantics unknown.

fields.name: post_array_word_b
fields.evidence: Second word after the sentinel array at copy 0x2C1C, immediately following post_array_word_a.

fields.name: zero_gap_2c20
fields.evidence: Zero gap scan-delimited by the 0xFF run starting at 0x2C5B.

fields.name: ff_sentinel_run
fields.evidence: Maximal 0xFF run measured exactly (start 0x2C5B, length 451). Odd length favours byte-sized empty-slot sentinels within the written template rather than erased SRAM, since the image is produced by the template flush.

fields.name: zero_gap_2e1e
fields.evidence: Zero gap between the 0xFF run and the 0xFFFF pair array (scan-delimited).

fields.name: ffff_pair_array

observed_values.sav-00-f990.sav: 48 entries of (u16_le 0xFFFF, u16_le 0x0000) = ff ff 00 00 repeated, 0x2FE4..0x30A3

fields.evidence: Pattern is exact over the whole span (48 repetitions). 0xFFFF reads as an unset ID paired with a zero value; semantics unknown.

fields.name: ff_stride4_array
fields.evidence: 4-byte stride is exact over the whole span. Could be 56 byte-flags in 4-byte records; the u32 type assignment is structural only.

fields.name: nibble_field_a
fields.evidence: Nibble-repeated pattern suggests eight packed 4-bit fields rather than a scalar; no field-level code access traced.

fields.name: nibble_field_b
fields.evidence: Immediately follows nibble_field_a; may be a 4-bit count/mask or the tail of a joint 8-byte bitfield block. Unproven.

fields.name: zero_gap_318c
fields.evidence: Zero gap before the 0x07 byte at 0x32EB (scan-delimited).

fields.name: byte_32eb
fields.evidence: Single non-zero byte immediately before the 12-byte record array. Ambiguous alignment: standalone count byte (=7) or top byte of a u32_le at 0x32E8 (0x07000000). No code resolves it.

fields.name: records12_array

observed_values.sav-00-f990.sav: 123 records of 12 bytes (u32_le 2, u32_le 0, u32_le 0) at 0x32EC + i*12 for i=0..122, ending 0x38B0 exclusive

fields.evidence: Stride-12 parse is exact: 123 records, first u32 always 2, remaining 8 bytes zero. The leading 2 reads as a default type/state enum per entry; what the entries represent is unknown.

fields.name: zero_gap_38b0
fields.evidence: Zero gap between the record array and the signature (scan-delimited).

fields.name: signature_title_sjis
fields.update_mechanism: Written as part of the whole-image template flush; verified on load by 0x0809dbe4 via FUN_08168564(a, b, 0x28). Corruption triggers whole-image repair.
fields.evidence: Bytes verified in both copies; exactly 40 bytes, matching the only length-0x28 SRAM verify call in the corpus, and the only text-like region in the file. Code-side offset is not provable because the verify operands are unresolved literal-pool placeholders, hence STATIC not VERIFIED for the code link.

fields.name: zero_tail_3a2c
fields.evidence: Trailing zero space between signature and checksum word; inside checksum coverage.

fields.name: checksum_stored

observed_values.sav-00-f990.sav: 0x2FB796B5 (bytes b5 96 b7 2f); identical at file offset 0x7FFC in copy 1

fields.update_mechanism: Recomputed as sum of u32_le words over copy 0x0000..0x3FFB mod 2^32 and rewritten on any flush; read back and compared by 0x0809dea0. Any payload mutation requires repairing this word in each copy that must validate.
fields.evidence: Python verification on the real file: computed 0x2FB796B5 == stored 0x2FB796B5 in both copies (see checksums entry). Code-side loop in FUN_0809dea0 accumulates the same sum over 16x0x400 chunks from 0x0E000000.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte of the stored checksum in copy 0 only; leave payload untouched
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_0809dea0 comparison fails, FUN_0809dbe4 rewrites the whole image from the template: progress lost, post-load .sav equals default template with a self-consistent checksum. Reload from sav-00-pre.ss (frame 1) to run the loader.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change one signature byte (0x82 -> 0x83 at copy offset 0x3A04), then repair the checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: FUN_08168564(...,0x28) verify fails despite valid checksum, triggering the same whole-image rewrite. If the save loads instead, the verified region is not at 0x3A04 and the signature-offset hypothesis is falsified.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt copy 1 payload and leave its checksum stale; keep copy 0 pristine
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Discriminator for redundancy: identical-to-known-good behaviour means copy 1 is never read (mirroring/artefact); repair, fallback, or any difference means copy 1 is a real backup read by untraced code. Compare against sav-00-post.ss/gameplay.ss behaviour.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set u32 at 0x1C20 from 1 to 0, then in a separate run from 1 to 2; repair checksum in both copies
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this is the status word returned by FUN_0809dbe4, the mode branch in 0x08112284 (object +0x78 = 1 vs 2, or the error path) changes visibly after boot. No change demotes it to an ordinary data field.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set u32 at 0x2C18 from 1 to 0 and u32 at 0x2C1C from 2 to 3 (separate runs); repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests the small-enum pair after the sentinel array as loader/game state words; a mode/count change localises which small word is consumed.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: In sentinel record 0 set first u16 999 -> 0; in a second run set its 30 u16s to 0..29; repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If 999 is an unset sentinel for per-entry scores/times/IDs, one UI entry becomes populated/changed while the other 33 records stay unset. No change suggests template filler.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If these are empty-slot IDs, one slot appears occupied/default-filled in the corresponding UI list; no effect indicates sentinel filler.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set entry 0 of the 48-entry pair array from (0xFFFF, 0) to (0x0001, 0); then set the paired halfword to 0x0063; repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: One (ID, value) entry becomes present wherever this table surfaces; the follow-up distinguishes ID presence from a count/amount in the second halfword.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change bytes 11 11 11 11 0F at 0x3184..0x3188 to 22 22 22 22 02; repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If packed 4-bit fields, several small settings/unlocks change at nibble granularity; a single scalar effect would favour a plain u32 reading.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set record 0 first u32 from 2 to 0, then to 5 (separate runs); repeat on the last record at copy offset 0x38A4; repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Tests the 123x12-byte record table and the default-state value 2: a per-entry state change confirms record boundaries and count 123; a crash/hang indicates a range-validated enum (record and revert).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set byte 0x32EB from 0x07 to 0x00, then to 0x7F; repair checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If a count for the neighbouring structure, truncated/extended list behaviour results; if it is the top byte of a u32 at 0x32E8, expect a large-value effect or none. Resolves the alignment ambiguity.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero the entire copy 0 payload (0x0000..0x3FFB) while keeping the signature intact and the checksum repaired and valid; mirror in copy 1
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Loader should accept the structurally valid but empty image (boot into empty-but-valid state). If it still rewrites, an extra validity condition exists beyond signature+checksum (e.g. the standalone status-word compare in FUN_0809dbe4); bisect by restoring regions 0x1C00, 0x2C18, 0x3A04 from the original.

open_questions: What is the RAM (EWRAM/IWRAM) base address of the save template struct? The writer source operand in FUN_0809dbe4/FUN_0809e00c is an unresolved Ghidra literal-pool placeholder (_DAT_0809dc7c class), so no field has a proven RAM mirror address.

Which on-save u32 does FUN_0809dbe4 read standalone and return to 0x08112284 (candidates: offsets 0x1C20, 0x2C18, 0x2C1C), what are its valid values, and which modes do they select (caller object fields +0x78/+0x7A)?

Who writes copy 1 at file offset 0x4000, if anyone? Traced code only addresses SRAM base 0x0E000000 for 0x4000 bytes: real backup by untraced code, 16 KiB SRAM mirroring, and imaging duplication all remain possible (fuzzing discriminator defined).

Where is the normal gameplay save path? No traced function mutates the save struct and flushes progress; either untraced code does it, or persistence happens only through the validate/repair whole-image rewrite.

What are the gameplay semantics of the structurally delimited regions (34x120-byte 999-sentinel records, 451-byte 0xFF run, 48 (0xFFFF,0) pairs, 56 stride-4 0xFF entries, 123x12-byte records with leading 2, nibble fields at 0x3184)? A second, progress-bearing .sav sample is needed.
Does untraced code ever address SRAM beyond 0x4000 (second slot or settings region), and is there any generation/sequence counter or copy-selection rule outside the traced corpus?

Is the 0x28-byte verified region in code exactly the Shift-JIS title at copy offset 0x3A04? The length match and uniqueness make it overwhelmingly likely, but the verify operands are unresolved placeholders, so the code-to-offset link is CONFIRMED_STATIC rather than CONFIRMED_VERIFIED.
